text:
incident-bot: [P1] Canary latency spike detected in canary-west-2-a. 95th/99th token latencies > 600ms vs baseline 120ms. rate of affected requests ~12% over last 5m. alert-rule: canary-tail-latency-crossed. triggered_at=2005004321
Sara (oncall): Paging. I’m on it. grabbing traces and will triage.
Alex (eng-runtime): I’m looking at recent deploys — there was a small scheduler change merged in the last deploy (commit 1a2f3b4) that touched worker-affinity and batching heuristics. Rolling back as a safety if we confirm.
Marta (eng-sre): Confirmed canary pool nodes showing context-switch bursts and CPU steal on a subset of pods. Looks correlated to the new scheduler flags.
Raj (eng-platform): Can we flip the feature flag for the scheduler to the previous behavior? flag: scheduler_v2_enabled (canary).
Samir (cs): Heads-up: we’ve seen ~6 customer 500s tied to long tails in the past 10m, customers A/B. No major page for SLOs yet but CS is tracking.
Sara (oncall): @Raj please kill the flag for canary. If we need faster: revert the single commit. Which is safer?
Raj (eng-platform): Killing the flag now: /feature-toggle set scheduler_v2_enabled=false --env=canary-west-2-a --user=raj
deploy-bot: feature-toggle scheduler_v2_enabled false applied to canary-west-2-a by raj at 2005004402. 8/10 canary pods updated.
Alex (eng-runtime): After the flag flip some nodes dropped latency quickly, but 2 pods still showing high tail. digging into kernel config and container runtime.
Marta (eng-sre): Rolling log snippet: ```
[2005004415] worker[7] batch_loop: scheduling delay=420ms, cpu_wait=380ms
[2005004420] worker[3] batch_loop: scheduling delay=610ms, cpu_wait=590ms
```
Sara (oncall): Can we cordon and restart the two affected pods? If they’re stuck in a bad state a restart will be faster than a full revert.
Alex (eng-runtime): Agree. Doing `kubectl rollout restart deploy/canary-runtime -l canary=west-2-a --grace-period=0` on the two pods. ETA ~60s.
deploy-bot: restart triggered for pod runtime-canary-7 and runtime-canary-3 by Alex at 2005004520.
Alex (eng-runtime): Restarts completed. Observability: 99th token latency down to 150ms, 95th ~90ms. Looks like restarts cleared the stuck kernel scheduling.
Samir (cs): Customer impact: 14 errors reported in last 30m, most transient. Notified top 2 affected customers and opened tickets.
Marta (eng-sre): Root cause hypothesis: scheduler_v2 change increased scheduling jitter under certain host kernel versions (5.15.*) leading to occasional long CPU waits for worker threads. Repro on staging with specific kernel+config.
Raj (eng-platform): We should still revert the commit from the previous roll to avoid recurring risk in other regions. I can do a single-commit revert to the canary branch: `git revert --no-edit 1a2f3b4 && git push origin canary` then trigger a patch release.
Alex (eng-runtime): Hold on — revert + release will take longer and we already mitigated canary. Can we instead pin the flag off in production rollout pipeline until we validate fixes? That will prevent accidental promotion.
Sara (oncall): Agreed. Action items: 1) Raj keep flag off for all rollouts and block promotion from canary. 2) Alex & Marta reproduce on staging and prepare minimal patch (kernel-compat guard) 3) Samir continue customer comms. 4) I’ll update incident timeline and mark P1 watch until next 2h.
Raj (eng-platform): Done: promotion blocked in release pipeline at 2005004680. Flag remains false for all envs.
Alex (eng-runtime): Started a minimal code patch branch that checks host kernel and disables the changed path when kernel in vulnerable set. Patch is a one-line guard, will open PR now.
Alex (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/987 (patch: kernel guard). CI quick checks pass.
Marta (eng-sre): Suggest we do a hotfix patch release to canary then run extended soak 1h, then if clean we can merge to main with revert or keep guard.
Raj (eng-platform): If patch is single commit we can do a canary hotpatch: `git cherry-pick 9f8e7d6 && deploy --env=canary-west-2-a --tag=hotfix-200500`
Sara (oncall): I’ll handoff to the daytime oncall in 20min — @Marta you’ll own watch during business hours?
Marta (eng-sre): I can take the handoff and keep an eye on telemetry. Please post quick summary and status.
Sara (oncall): Summary: incident triggered by canary scheduler change -> flag killed -> two pods restarted -> latencies returned to near baseline. Promotion pipeline blocked. Hotfix PR opened for kernel-compat guard. Customer impact limited/transient. Marking incident state: mitigated, watch.
Samir (cs): I’m updating customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full patch. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident state updated to MITIGATED by Sara at 2005004800.
Marta (eng-sre): Taking over watch. Will update if any regression in next hour.
Sara (oncall): Thanks all, good job.
